paper.title: Data Dependent Regret Guarantees Against General Comparators for Full or Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Full feedback setting (prediction with expert advice against general comparator sequences)
unmapped: Regret measured against an arbitrary comparator sequence S_T from a user-designed competition class (fixed arms, switching, contextual, periodic) with complexity W(Lambda_T) <= W; the learner uses the complexity bound W
Losses are arbitrary real numbers with no known range; bounds depend on realized per-round loss ranges
settings.definition_quote: the full feedback setting, in which we observe the loss of each expert, i.e., $l_{t,m}, \forall m$ irrespective of the selection $i_t$ that we made; ... Let the expected regret against $S_T$ be $R_{S_T} =\E\left[C_{I_T} - C_{S_T}\right]$, where the expectation is over the selections $I_T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit feedback setting (against general comparator sequences)
unmapped: Regret measured against an arbitrary comparator sequence S_T from a user-designed competition class with complexity W(Lambda_T) <= W; the learner uses the complexity bound W
Losses are arbitrary real numbers with no known range; bounds depend on realized per-round loss ranges
settings.definition_quote: the bandit feedback setting, where only the loss of the selected expert $i_t$, i.e., $l_{t,i_t}$ is observed. In both cases, our objective is to minimize regret, which is defined as the difference between our cumulative loss and that of a strategy chosen from the set of comparators.

conditions: comparator sequence Lambda_T has complexity W(Lambda_T) <= W

source.label: thm:11
source.quote: When using \autoref{alg:framework} with the selection in \autoref{rem:sec1}, we have R_T(\Lambda_T)\leq 2(1+W)\max_{1\leq t\leq T}\triangle_t+2\sqrt{W\sum_{t=1}^T\triangle_t^2}, where $\triangle_t=\max_m l_{t,m}- \min_{m} l_{t,m}$.

results.notes: Comparator is an arbitrary sequence from a designed competition class (not only switching); best_switching_sequence is the closest vocabulary value. Regret R_T is expectation over the learner's randomization against a fixed comparator sequence.
